topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
source_evidence: Some funds call themselves no-expense or zero-expense funds or emphasize their low expense ratios without mentioning other costs investors pay—either directly or indirectly— when investing in the fund.
answer: A fund described as “zero-expense” may still involve costs. Some costs may be paid separately, such as a broker commission or an adviser fee, while others—such as certain securities-lending or trading costs—may not appear in the fund’s expense ratio. These costs can still reduce the value of your investment, so look beyond the zero-expense label when reviewing a fund’s costs.
